notes:
Account overview: Arcadia builds a mid-market billing/subscription product for vertical SaaS (HR/payroll apps). Currently ~350 employees, HQ in Boston. Primary need: customer-support chat assistant that surfaces billing state and can trigger Stripe/Zuora operations (create invoice, issue refund, change plan).

Recent timeline (bulleted):
- 2025-11-12: AE intro call (Jordan) — high-level fit, they struggle with response SLAs for live support.
- 2026-01-18: Tech deep-dive with SE (Priya) — architecture, data-flow, compliance requirements.
- 2026-02-12: Hosted API demo (streaming + function-calls) — pilot confirmed feasibility for tool-calls. (ff_2026-02-12_Arcadia-Intro)
- 2026-02-22: POC kickoff, ingest sample Stripe webhooks, mapped Zuora billing schema, whitebox latency tests started (ff_2026-02-22_POC-demo).
- 2026-02-28: POC mid-check; developer feedback: JSON schema outputs reliable but p95 first-byte latency spikes during peak simulated traffic. Gmail threads attached.

POC scope / acceptance criteria: 
- Workload: chat agent used by Tier 1 support to handle billing tickets and live chat; typical session length 6-12 messages.
- Integrations: Stripe (primary), Zuora (legacy customers). Tool calls to execute: create_charge, refund_payment, fetch_invoice, update_subscription. All actions must return a validated JSON payload matching Arcadia's internal schema.
- Performance targets: p95 first-byte latency <= 200ms for streaming start; end-to-end transaction (including tool call) <= 650ms ideally. Sustained concurrency target: 150 concurrent sessions, burst to 300. Monthly expected usage: ~200k chat sessions, ~2M generated tokens.
- Quality: structured-output success rate (valid JSON + fields present) >= 98% on test harness. Tool-call safety checks and idempotency headers required.
- Security/compliance: SSO/SAML integration for agents, audit logging of all tool-calls, KMS for envelope encryption of customer identifiers, GDPR residency for EU customers (data residency flagged).

Notes from last calls: 
- "We can't accept >200ms p95 for the streaming start — customers notice choppy typing and it kills CSAT" (Head of Support paraphrase).
- Engineering: concerned about token cost at scale; want Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching and KV caching.
- Product: prioritized JSON-first responses because downstream workflow automation ingests the assistant output directly.

Technical POC details: 
- Running POC on Redwood Hosted API initially. Test harness simulates Stripe webhooks + chat front-end; function-call responses stubbed to call a sandbox Stripe account.
- Observed pattern: cold KV cache + long-form invoice retrieval causes latency spikes; SE recommended prefix caching and shorter context windows for billing flows.
- Fallback policy: prefer smaller quantized variant for low-priority background tasks; require deterministic rollbacks if function-call fails.

Commercial / procurement notes: 
- Interested in pricing for Hosted API (pay-as-you-go) during POC; Dedicated pricing requested if latency SLOs validated — customer prefers committed monthly with reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput.
- Legal requested SOC2 Type II report and data processing addendum before Dedicated procurement.

Next steps (short): 
- Jordan to send updated pricing sheet and SLA matrix by 2026-03-03 (actioned).
- Priya to run focused latency sweep with caching enabled; deliver p95 report 2026-03-07.
- Arcadia engineering to provide final Zuora schema mapping and success/error codes by 2026-03-10 (blocker until schema approved).

Stubs / links: pricing deck + security questionnaire attached to Drive; Fireflies transcripts for demo calls.

Sales play notes: good fit for Hosted->Dedicated motion: start hosted, validate streaming + function-calls, then upsell to Dedicated reserved capacity if p95 SLA and deterministic tool-calls validated. Emphasize Redwood Optimize savings (quantization + batching) to hit their ARR targets.

Contact cadence: weekly syncs (Jordan+Priya), engineering deep-dive every other Wednesday.
